doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: The 'good and bad thing about your technique' quote
summary: He explains the remark quoted in Bill Crow's book, that technique is only the bottom rung of the ladder.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I read a quote that was attributed to you, and I wondered if it was correct. Something you said to a student about technique?
Oh, you’re talking about Bill Crow’s book, yeah.

Oh I said the good thing about you is your technique. The bad thing about you is your technique. Something along those lines. I never realized I’d said it until after it, but I got quoted by students who said, “Do you remember what you told me back in camp, back in such and such” and I said oh boy, here I go again you know.
Yeah, I guess too much technique can be dangerous if you don’t know exactly what to do with it.
Well that’s the ultimate priority, because technique is only the bottom rung of the ladder. Music is much more than its functional parts.
